title: Section 3: Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation, Physiotherapy & Occupational Therapy

content.text: The core objective of multidisciplinary SCI rehabilitation is to maximize functional independence, mitigate secondary medical complications, optimize community reintegration, and maintain long-term physical and psychological health.

sections.heading: Categories of Physical Activity in SCI

content.text: 1. Physical Activity & Rehabilitation Awareness 🟡 CLINICAL REVIEW NOT CONDUCTED – PROFESSIONAL GUIDANCE REQUIRED

items: Physical activity and rehabilitation after SCI may include general mobility, strengthening, flexibility, and balance concepts. All specific exercise routines, transfer techniques, and physical therapy plans must be individually prescribed and supervised by a qualified clinician or physiotherapist.

content.text: Occupational Therapy focuses on enabling individuals to participate in meaningful daily activities (Activities of Daily Living - ADLs) and fostering personal independence:

items: Self-Care & ADL Training: Instruction and adaptation for dressing, grooming, bathing, feeding, and hygiene management.

Upper-Limb & Hand Function Concepts: General occupational therapy strategies may explore strengthening, tenodesis grip principles, and splinting to optimize upper extremity function. Readers must consult qualified occupational therapists for individualized upper-limb assessments and interventions.
Adaptive Equipment Selection: Evaluation and training in specialized eating utensils, button hooks, reachers, and adaptive technology.
Environmental & Home Modification: Assessing living, learning, and work environments to recommend accessibility adjustments and ergonomic layouts.
